system.name: The Tell-Tale Norm
system.one_liner: Shows that the ℓ2 norm of hidden states tracks layer-wise reasoning intensity in LLMs, then uses it to steer and select reasoning at test time.

content.variant_note: one hidden-state collection stage on top, two parallel analysis cards below (each with a trend chart and a bold takeaway); the reasoning vs non-reasoning contrast runs through every part
content.argues: Reasoning activity intensifies in late layers, visible both in SAE reasoning-feature activations and in the hidden-state ℓ2 norm, which therefore faithfully indicates reasoning intensity.
content.subject: Layer-wise hidden states of reasoning versus non-reasoning responses, analysed with an SAE and with the ℓ2 norm as trend charts.

lessons.what_to_learn: Run one colour contrast (bright = the phenomenon, grey = the baseline) through every part of an analysis figure - cards, state stacks, icons, plot lines - so no legend is needed, and close each analysis card with a one-line bold takeaway and a pictogram.
lessons.suits: interpretability or analysis findings that compare an active case with a baseline across several measurements and end in one-sentence claims.

evidence: reasoning activity intensifies in the later layers, which is reflected by SAE feature activations and hidden state ℓ2 norms
demonstrating that the ℓ2 norm of hidden states serves as an endogenous signal of the model’s reasoning intensity

summary: The paper argues that the ℓ2 norm of an LLM's hidden states is an intrinsic signal of reasoning intensity, checks it with sparse autoencoder (SAE) features as a probe, and then builds three training-free test-time scaling techniques on it. Figure 1 is a three-part composite in dashed frames. The top panel passes one prompt through a reasoning response and a non-reasoning response into an LLM drawn as layer boxes with a hidden-state stack, and collects yellow (reasoning) and grey (non-reasoning) state stacks marked with lit and dark bulbs. Below, two analysis cards put an SAE box (flame icon) and a norm box (snowflake icon) beside layer-index trend charts and end with a bold one-line takeaway. Bright colour versus grey carries the contrast throughout; icons are stock clip art and text is serif.
summary_zh: 论文指出大模型隐状态的 ℓ2 范数可作为推理强度的内生信号，并以 SAE 特征为探针验证。图分三块虚线框：上方收集推理与非推理回答的逐层隐状态，下方两张分析卡各配趋势图与一句结论，亮色对灰色贯穿全图。
notes: The prior label concept-schematic was dropped because the trend charts are measured bitmaps (listed under pictures), not a schematic; side-by-side-contrast was added for the reasoning vs non-reasoning lanes. The brain icon at the prompt is read as the LLM. The stray clipped 'Non-Reasoning States' text in Analysis 2 appears in the text layer as a second copy of the top label. Width value 'column' is used for a single-column figure (the schema example only shows 'full').
